title: SET teachers’ reported school sit-ins and related 72-hour strike over detained colleagues
location: Unspecified schools in Togo; no individual school or sit-in location is named.
scope: The report describes the strike as nationwide but only places sit-ins at some unspecified schools; the geographic extent of those sit-ins is unknown.
organizer: Syndicat des Enseignants du Togo (SET), as attributed by the report; sit-in organizer(s) at individual schools are not separately identified.
participants_original: Teachers reportedly observed a nationwide 72-hour strike; sit-ins reportedly took place at some schools. No attendance number or estimate is given.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. The article reports sit-ins at some schools but gives no school count, crowd estimate, or attendance at any site. A nationwide strike claim does not establish 50 people at a public gathering.

title.summary: Lome Gazette reports sit-ins at some schools alongside a 72-hour teacher strike; it does not establish whether these were one coordinated physical episode or separate tactics.

start_date.summary: The report gives relative phrases (“since Monday” for sit-ins and “since yesterday Tuesday” for the strike), but its publication date is Friday 22 January 2021. Preserve month precision because the relative chronology conflicts.

end_date.summary: The report describes a 72-hour strike, but the start-date conflict prevents a reliable end date; the sit-ins’ duration and physical end are not reported.

location.summary: The article places sit-ins at unspecified schools. It does not name schools or identify specific gathering sites.

scope.summary: The report characterizes the strike as nationwide but says sit-ins were taking place in some schools; the geographic extent of the sit-ins is not established.

organizer.summary: The reports attribute the labor action to the Syndicat des Enseignants du Togo (SET); the inspected sources do not establish the organizer of each school sit-in separately.

demands.summary: The immediate demand reported is release of detained SET colleagues. It is provisionally mapped to labor_wage_dispute as a union labor-rights demand; the source does not give a detailed demand platform for the sit-ins.

participants_original.summary: Teachers are reported on strike nationwide and sit-ins at some schools, but no participant count or estimate is provided.

participants_min.summary: No numerical lower bound is reported; the record does not establish 50 participants at any gathering.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Occurrence of sit-ins is reported, but neither attendance, a number of participating schools, nor wording that clearly establishes 50 people at any single gathering is provided. Threshold remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not describe conduct at the sit-ins; protester violence remains unknown.

state_response.summary: The inspected reporting contains no event-specific state response to the reported sit-ins/strike. The 20 January union-office arrests predate the reported action and are not coded as its response; later official warnings concern announced actions, not a verified response to this event. All seven dimensions remain unknown. S052 separately documents the 22 January ministerial letter and school-monitoring request, but ties it to planned strike activity, not a verified response to the sit-ins.

eligibility.summary: A labor action and school sit-ins are reported, but the protocol’s public-gathering ≥50-person threshold is not established; pending threshold review.

notes: Lome Gazette’s 22 January report is the only opened source reviewed that states sit-ins were actually taking place, while also reporting a 72-hour strike. Its relative-date wording conflicts with the dated article, and the report gives no headcount or named school. Later coverage concerns different announced strike dates, cancellation or suspension, and official warnings; those plans are not merged into this report. The immediate demand is described as release of detained SET colleagues; the labor_wage_dispute taxonomy mapping is provisional. Earlier arrests at a union-office meeting are not treated as event response.
open_questions: Did any individual sit-in reach 50 participants, and how many schools/sites were involved?
What were the exact dates of the sit-ins and the 72-hour strike given the weekday conflict?
Were the sit-ins organized by SET nationally, by local branches, or independently at schools?
Were the sit-ins and work stoppage one episode or separate tactics/actions?
Was there an event-specific state response to the actual sit-ins or strike?
Does the official coding procedure map the immediate release-of-unionists demand to labor_wage_dispute?
